title: Why Pendulums Keep Time
subject: science
description: Discover what sets a pendulum's rhythm by experimenting — then use it to fix a clock and visit the Moon.

steps.prompt: You hang a heavier weight on the same pendulum. One full swing (the period) will take…

misconceptions.0: Most people guess this! Heavier things feel slower — let's test it.
misconceptions.1: Gravity pulls harder on heavy things, but there's also more mass to move. Let's test it.

steps.explain: Let's find out with a real experiment.

steps.goal: Try at least 3 different masses and watch the period readout.

steps.title: Mass cancels out
steps.text: Gravity pulls a heavier bob **harder**, but a heavier bob is also **harder to accelerate**. The two effects cancel exactly — so the period doesn't depend on mass.

steps.prompt: A 1 kg and a 5 kg bob hang on identical 1 m strings. Which swings faster?
steps.explain: Period depends on length and gravity, not mass.

steps.prompt: Now make the string longer. The period will…

misconceptions.1: A longer string means a longer arc to travel — so each swing takes more time.
misconceptions.2: Unlike mass, length really matters. Try it!

steps.goal: Tune the pendulum so one full swing takes 2.0 seconds.

steps.title: The formula
steps.text: The period is **T = 2π√(L/g)** — L is the length, g ≈ 9.81 m/s² is gravity. Mass doesn't appear at all.

steps.prompt: What is the period of a 1 m pendulum on Earth? (g = 9.81 m/s²)
steps.explain: T = 2π√(1/9.81) ≈ 2.01 s. That's why old clocks use pendulums about 1 m long.

steps.title: Grandfather clocks
steps.text: A pendulum clock counts swings. If its pendulum swings **too slowly**, the clock falls behind.

steps.prompt: A pendulum clock is running slow. How do you fix it?
steps.explain: Shorter pendulum → shorter period → faster ticking.

misconceptions.2: Mass doesn't change the period — you discovered that last lesson!

steps.prompt: You take the clock to the Moon, where gravity is 6× weaker. The clock will run…

misconceptions.0: Weaker gravity pulls the bob back more gently, so each swing takes longer.
misconceptions.2: g is in the formula — gravity matters, unlike mass.

steps.explain: Smaller g → bigger L/g → longer period → slower clock.

steps.goal: On the Moon (g = 1.62): make the pendulum tick every 2.0 s again.

steps.prompt: How long must a pendulum be on the Moon for a 2.0 s period? (g = 1.62 m/s²)
steps.explain: L = g·(T/2π)² = 1.62 × (2/2π)² ≈ 0.164 m — about 6× shorter than on Earth.
